settings.title: Settings
settings.regressionValueDescription: The regression value determines how much a song's priority is reduced when it moves down (default: 0.1). After 10 regressions, priority is reduced by 1.0.
settings.customUrlDescription: When set, the QR code will be generated with this URL + "/new". When empty, the current domain is used automatically.
settings.overlayTitleDescription: This title is displayed in the QR code overlay at the /show endpoint.
settings.showProjectionModeDescription: Hides QR code, logo, singer names, song title, and top/bottom bars on /show. Only video, lyrics, and progress bars remain visible — ideal for projectors.
settings.youtubeEnabled: Allow YouTube links in song requests:
settings.youtubeEnabledDescription: When disabled, users can only select songs from the local song list. YouTube links are not accepted.
settings.autoApproveSongsDescription: When enabled, song requests are automatically added to the playlist. When disabled, song requests that are either YouTube songs (not cached) or on the invisible list are submitted for manual approval.
settings.cloudflaredDescription: Cloudflared creates a secure tunnel to your local server. After starting, a public URL is automatically generated and set as "Custom URL".
settings.usdbCredentialsDescription: Credentials for the UltraStar Database (usdb.animux.de). These are required to download songs from USDB.
settings.confirmDeleteUsdbCredentials: Do you really want to delete the USDB credentials?
settings.localSongFolderDescription: Folder with local karaoke videos in "Artist - Song Title.extension" format. These songs have highest priority in recognition.
settings.localWebServerDescription: Start a local web server so videos can be played via HTTP
settings.allSongsRemovedSuccess: All songs successfully removed from list!
settings.pleaseSpecifySongFolder: Please specify a song folder first
settings.usdbSearchEnabled: Enable USDB search in song requests:
settings.usdbSearchEnabledDescription: When enabled, songs from USDB (UltraStar Database) will also be searched and displayed when searching for songs in song requests.
settings.paypalDonationsIntro: Configure PayPal so guests can tip from /new. Values are stored in the database. Environment variables still work as fallback if a field is empty (except the client secret, which only comes from DB or env on server).
settings.paypalPublicUrlHint: HTTPS URL without trailing slash (e.g. https://karaoke.example.com). Used for PayPal return and cancel redirects.
settings.paypalWebhookUrlHint: Built from your public base URL. Enter this exact URL in the PayPal Developer Dashboard under Webhooks (HTTPS).
settings.paypalWebhookUrlEmpty: Please fill in the public base URL first.
settings.paypalClientSecretHint: Leave empty only if Client ID and Sandbox/Live did not change — otherwise the old secret stays in the database (common cause of invalid_client in live). After switching to Live, paste the Live secret from the Developer Dashboard and save.
settings.paypalWebhookHint: From PayPal Developer → Webhooks. Required for signature verification in production.
settings.paypalQuickAmountsHint: Chips below the amount field on /new, e.g. 1, 5, 10. Empty list = manual entry only. Up to 20 values (1–500 each).
settings.paypalSandboxHint: On = api.sandbox.paypal.com and sandbox credentials. Off = live payments.
settings.paypalLiveHint: Live mode: copy Client ID and Secret from the Developer Dashboard’s Live tab (not Sandbox) and save here. Sandbox and live credentials differ — “invalid_client” usually means sandbox credentials are still stored or the secret is wrong.
settings.donationDisplayTitle: Donation display on the big screen (/show)
settings.donationDisplayIntro: Shown on the Show tab (top ticker and short overlay after a donation). Saved together with PayPal donation settings.
settings.donationMarqueeTemplateHint: Placeholder: {names} — all donors this session, joined with spaces, your separator, and spaces (e.g. “Alex +++ Jordan”).
settings.donationMarqueeSeparatorHint: Default: +++. Shown as space–separator–space between names.
settings.donationNotificationTemplateHint: Placeholder: {name} — the donor who just contributed.
settings.donationNewPageThankYouHint: Green message after a successful PayPal donation. Empty / whitespace only = built-in translation (e.g. “Thank you for your support! …”).
settings.donationShowButtonOnNewPageLabel: Donation button on the request page (/new)
settings.donationShowButtonOnNewPageVisible: Visible — guests see the donation button below the form.
settings.donationShowButtonOnNewPageHidden: Hidden — paying by direct link still works; the button is not shown.
settings.donationShowButtonOnNewPageHint: Visibility on /new only. PayPal must still be configured for donations to work.
settings.paypalGuideAccountP1: For live donations through the PayPal REST API (as Titanium Kitten uses), you almost always need a business-facing PayPal account – typically a Business account or whatever seller/business type PayPal requires in your country. A plain personal consumer account is usually not sufficient to accept payments on your own website through the REST API.
settings.paypalGuideAccountP2: For testing without real money, use Sandbox: in the PayPal Developer Dashboard you create an app and use the Sandbox Client ID and Secret with the Sandbox checkbox enabled in Titanium Kitten.
settings.paypalGuideAccountP3: Exact requirements may vary by country – if unsure, check PayPal’s official docs or support for “website payments” / Business accounts.
settings.paypalGuideMappingIntro: The left column is the field name in Titanium Kitten. The right column tells you where the value comes from in PayPal or if it is only set here.
settings.paypalGuideRowPublic: Not a single field you copy from PayPal. Enter your site’s public HTTPS base URL (no trailing slash), often the same as “Custom URL” or your tunnel URL. PayPal uses it via the API for return URLs after payment.
settings.paypalGuideRowClientId: PayPal: developer.paypal.com → Dashboard → Apps & Credentials → select or create an app → Sandbox or Live tab → copy “Client ID”. Titanium Kitten: paste into “REST API Client ID”. Sandbox and Live IDs differ – use Sandbox credentials when Sandbox mode is on in Titanium Kitten.
settings.paypalGuideRowSecret: PayPal: same app as Client ID → show or generate “Secret” and copy immediately (often shown only once). Titanium Kitten: “REST API Secret”; leave empty to keep an already saved secret.
settings.paypalGuideRowWebhook: PayPal: Dashboard → Apps & Credentials → your app → Webhooks → webhook URL exactly: your public base URL + “/api/donations/paypal-webhook” (HTTPS). Subscribe to e.g. PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED. After saving, copy the Webhook ID from the list. Titanium Kitten: “Webhook ID” field.
settings.paypalGuideRowCurrency: Set only in Titanium Kitten. PayPal receives the currency on each payment via the API. It must match your PayPal account and product setup.
settings.paypalGuideRowAmount: Titanium Kitten only: suggested default amount on the request page. PayPal sees the actual amount at checkout; it is sent when the order is created.
settings.paypalGuideRowBrand: Titanium Kitten only: shown as the brand name on PayPal’s payment page. There is no separate required field for it in the Developer Dashboard.
settings.paypalGuideRowSandbox: Titanium Kitten: when enabled, payments go to PayPal Sandbox (test). PayPal: use Sandbox Client ID and Secret from the Sandbox tab of the same app; for live, turn off Sandbox and use Live credentials.
settings.playlistLogDescription: Records song requests, fairness placement, admin reorders, and follow-ups (USDB, cache, downloads).
